name: Wheel of Heaven Flood-Myth Concordance
description: A comparative table of the ancient Near Eastern and Indo-European flood traditions — survivor, decreeing power, warner, cause, vessel, birds, landing place, and aftermath — with links to the digitized source texts. CC0 public domain.

rows.cause: The assembly's sworn decision to wipe out humankind
rows.aftermath: Ziusudra granted eternal life; settled in Dilmun

rows.vessel: A roofed reed boat sealed with pitch
rows.aftermath: The gods regret it; Enlil institutes mortality and birth controls

rows.cause: The gods' decision to destroy humankind
rows.vessel: A seven-decked cube-shaped boat sealed with pitch
rows.birds_released: Dove, swallow, raven (the raven does not return)
rows.aftermath: Sacrifice; the gods gather “like flies”; Utnapishtim and wife granted immortality

rows.cause: The wickedness of humankind; “the earth was filled with violence”
rows.vessel: A gopher-wood ark, three decks, pitched inside and out
rows.birds_released: A raven, then a dove released three times
rows.aftermath: Burnt offering; the rainbow covenant never to flood the earth again

rows.warned_by: Allah (Nuh preaches; the ark built under revelation)
rows.cause: The people's persistent rejection of Nuh's warning
rows.vessel: The ark, built “under Our eyes and Our inspiration”
rows.aftermath: The disbelievers drown, including Nuh's own son; “O earth, swallow up thy water”

rows.cause: Zeus's resolve to destroy the men of the Bronze Age
rows.aftermath: Repopulation by casting stones — “the bones of their mother” — over the shoulder

rows.vessel: An enormous boat (five stadia by two)
rows.birds_released: Birds released three times (return; return muddied; do not return)
rows.aftermath: Xisuthros, wife, daughter and pilot translated to dwell with the gods

rows.vessel: A boat tied to the fish's horn
rows.landing_place: The northern mountain (the “descent of the north”)
rows.aftermath: Manu, sole survivor, generates humankind again through Iḍā

rows.cause: The end of the Fourth Sun (Nahui-Atl, ‘4-Water’); the age destroyed by flood
rows.aftermath: They roast the drowned people (now fish); the smoke angers the star-gods, and Tezcatlipoca turns Tata and Nena into dogs

rows.source_text: Betanzos, Suma y narración de los Incas; Molina, Relación de las fábulas y ritos de los Incas
rows.survivor: A man and a woman sealed in a box
rows.cause: Viracocha destroys the first race (a race of giants) for disobedience
rows.aftermath: Viracocha refashions humanity from stone at Tiwanaku and repopulates the earth

rows.approx_date: c. 1220 CE (Prose Edda); older eddic verse
rows.cause: The blood of the slain primordial giant Ymir floods the world, drowning the frost giants
rows.vessel: A lúðr (a hollowed tree-trunk), on Snorri's reading
rows.aftermath: Bergelmir and his wife survive to continue the race of frost giants (jötnar)
